code: library(dkge)  wts_adapt <- dkge_weights(   prior   = NULL,            # no prior information   adapt   = "kenergy_prec",  # energy × precision, a simple SNR proxy   combine = "product",   mix     = 0.6,             # adaptive term has more influence than the prior   shrink  = list(alpha = 0.5, winsor = 0.99, normalize = "mean"),   scope   = "fold"           # recomputed on the training subjects of each fold )  print(wts_adapt) #> dkge weight specification #>   prior   : uniform  #>   adapt   : kenergy_prec (scope = fold ) #>   combine : product (mix = 0.60 ) #>   shrink  : alpha =0.50, winsor =0.990, normalize =mean make_subject <- function(id, q = 4L, v = 60L) {   design <- diag(q)   colnames(design) <- paste0("eff", seq_len(q))   beta <- matrix(rnorm(q * v), nrow = q)   dkge_subject(beta, design = design, id = paste0("sub", id)) }  subjects <- lapply(seq_len(10L), make_subject) K <- diag(4)  fit_uniform  <- dkge(subjects, K = K, rank = 2, w_method = "none") fit_adaptive <- dkge(subjects, K = K, rank = 2, weights = wts_adapt) head(fit_adaptive$voxel_weights) #> cluster_1 cluster_2 cluster_3 cluster_4 cluster_5 cluster_6  #>     0.904     0.983     0.930     1.236     0.882     0.931 dkge_diagnostics(fit_adaptive)$voxel_weights #> $mean #> [1] 1 #>  #> $sd #> [1] 0.132 #>  #> $min #> [1] 0.862 #>  #> $max #> [1] 1.44

title: Feature-Anchored DKGE
text: example simulates three subjects. item features, sampled around four latent prototypes, clusters, two subjects share parcellation.
code: # Number of latent anchors and feature dimension d <- 20L anchors_true <- matrix(rnorm(4 * d), 4, d)  make_subject <- function(n_items, n_vox, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   # Each subject observes item features around the latent anchors   centers <- anchors_true[sample.int(nrow(anchors_true), n_items, replace = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]   features <- centers + matrix(rnorm(n_items * d, sd = 0.4), n_items, d)    # Build an item similarity kernel (e.g., RSA over betas)   latent <- matrix(rnorm(n_items * 3), n_items, 3)   beta_loadings <- matrix(rnorm(3 * n_vox), 3, n_vox)   betas <- latent %*% beta_loadings + matrix(rnorm(n_items * n_vox, sd = 0.2), n_items, n_vox)   item_kernel <- betas %*% t(betas)    list(features = features,        item_kernel = item_kernel) }  subjects <- list(   s1 = make_subject(30, 120, seed = 11),   s2 = make_subject(45, 120, seed = 12),   s3 = make_subject(35, 120, seed = 13) )  features_list <- lapply(subjects, `[[`, "features") K_item_list  <- lapply(subjects, `[[`, "item_kernel")

code: factors <- list(cond = list(L = 2), time = list(L = 4)) kern    <- design_kernel(factors, basis = "effect") q       <- nrow(kern$K)   # number of effect-coded columns q #> [1] 7 n_subjects <- 10L v <- 60L  make_subject <- function(id) {   # design: identity matrix over effects (one trial per effect)   design <- diag(q)   colnames(design) <- rownames(kern$K)    # signal: condition contrast (first effect column) drives voxels 1-10   signal <- matrix(0, nrow = q, ncol = v)   signal[1, 1:10] <- 0.5    # positive signal for condition contrast    beta <- signal + matrix(rnorm(q * v, sd = 1.0), nrow = q)   dkge_subject(beta, design = design, id = paste0("sub", id)) }  subjects <- lapply(seq_len(n_subjects), make_subject) fit <- dkge(subjects, K = kern, rank = 2) fit #> <dkge> #>   Subjects: 10  #>   Effects: 7  #>   Rank: 2  #>   Subject weighting: mfa_sigma1 (tau = 0.3)  #>   Weight range: 0.8058 to 1.1005 (median = 1.008, CV = 0.08452)  #>   Effective subject mass: 9.936 of 10 usable

code: # 4 effects: A_run1, A_run2, B_run1, B_run2 make_subject_multi <- function(id) {   design <- diag(4)   colnames(design) <- c("A_run1", "A_run2", "B_run1", "B_run2")    signal <- matrix(0, nrow = 4, ncol = v)   signal[1:2, 1:10] <-  0.5   # both A runs share signal   signal[3:4, 1:10] <- -0.5   # both B runs share the opposite signal    beta <- signal + matrix(rnorm(4 * v, sd = 1.0), nrow = 4)   dkge_subject(beta, design = design, id = paste0("sub", id)) }  subjects_multi <- lapply(seq_len(n_subjects), make_subject_multi) fit_multi      <- dkge(subjects_multi, K = diag(4), rank = 2)  # Weight matrix: rows = classes, columns = effects. # Each class averages its two runs. W_runs <- matrix(0, nrow = 2, ncol = 4) W_runs[1, 1:2] <- 0.5    # class A = mean(A_run1, A_run2) W_runs[2, 3:4] <- 0.5    # class B = mean(B_run1, B_run2) rownames(W_runs) <- c("A", "B") cls_multi <- dkge_classify(fit_multi,                            targets = W_runs,   # plain matrix dispatch                            mode = "cell_cross",                            n_perm  = 49,                            seed    = 101)  res_multi <- cls_multi$results[[1]] res_multi$metrics #>     accuracy      logloss  #> 1.000000e+00 9.999779e-13 as.data.frame(cls_multi) #>    target   metric        value p_value n_perm #> 1 target1 accuracy 1.000000e+00    0.02     49 #> 2 target1  logloss 9.999779e-13    0.02     49

code: library(dkge) S <- 4; q <- 5; P <- 18; T <- 70 effect_names <- paste0("effect", seq_len(q)) cluster_names <- paste0("cluster", seq_len(P)) cluster_axis <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = P) shared_signal <- rbind(   exp(-4 * (cluster_axis + 0.45)^2),   -exp(-4 * (cluster_axis - 0.45)^2),   cluster_axis,   rep(0, P),   rep(0, P) ) betas <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) {   B <- shared_signal + matrix(rnorm(q * P, sd = 0.35), q, P)   dimnames(B) <- list(effect_names, cluster_names)   B }) designs <- replicate(S, {   X <- matrix(rnorm(T * q), T, q)   X <- qr.Q(qr(X))   colnames(X) <- effect_names   X }, simplify = FALSE) subjects <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) dkge_subject(betas[[s]], designs[[s]], id = paste0("sub", s))) bundle <- dkge_data(subjects) fit <- dkge(bundle, K = diag(q), rank = 3) fit_jd <- dkge(bundle,                K = diag(q),                rank = 3,                solver = "jd",                jd_control = dkge_jd_control(maxit = 200, tol = 1e-8))

code: library(dkge) S <- 8; q <- 4; P <- 25; T <- 60 effect_names <- paste0("effect", seq_len(q)) cluster_axis <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = P) planted <- exp(-5 * (cluster_axis + 0.35)^2) -   0.65 * exp(-7 * (cluster_axis - 0.45)^2) truth <- matrix(0, q, P, dimnames = list(effect_names, NULL)) truth[1, ] <- planted / 2 truth[2, ] <- -planted / 2  betas <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) {   truth + matrix(rnorm(q * P, sd = 0.30), q, P) }) designs <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) {   X <- matrix(rnorm(T * q), T, q)   X <- qr.Q(qr(X))   colnames(X) <- effect_names   X }) reference_centroids <- cbind(x = 10 * cluster_axis, y = 0, z = 0) centroids <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) {   reference_centroids + matrix(rnorm(P * 3, sd = 0.02), P, 3) }) subjects <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) dkge_subject(betas[[s]], designs[[s]], id = paste0("sub", s))) bundle <- dkge_data(subjects) fit <- dkge(bundle, K = diag(q), rank = 3) fit$centroids <- centroids  # attach for transport helpers; pass explicitly in production

Default "cell". contrasts Optional named list per-factor contrast matrices used basis="effect". NULL, uses order terms. block_factors Optional factor names forced use factor kernel every cell-space term. gives block-diagonal replication across -subject factors group instead accidental -ones coupling terms omit block factor. normalize One "unit_trace", "none", "unit_fro", "max_diag". title: Compute DKGE contrasts with cross-fitting — dkge_contrast
text: function provides unified interface three cross-fitting strategies: LOSO (method = "loso"): Recomputes basis excluding subject, projects subject's data. gold standard unbiased estimation requires S eigen-decompositions. K-fold (method = "kfold"): Splits data K folds, recomputes basis excluding fold, projects held-data. efficient LOSO maintaining good bias properties. Supports time-based, run-based, custom fold definitions. Analytic (method = "analytic"): Uses first-order eigenvalue perturbation theory approximate LOSO solution without full recomputation. Fast may less accurate subjects high leverage. methods work entirely qxq design space respect K-metric throughout. semidefinite kernel defines quotient effect space: dkge_contrast() errors contrast lies wholly null(K), warns part contrast represented, reports transformed-query collisions metadata$kernel_query_pairs. Multiple contrasts can evaluated simultaneously efficiency. Exact fold replay currently supports fits made solver = "pooled" cpca_part = "none". CPCA joint-diagonalization fits fail closed three methods; DKGE replace fitted estimator ordinary pooled eigensolve calling result cross-fitted.

"mfa_sigma1" (default): inverse squared leading singular value \(K^{1/2} Btil_s H_s^{T} \Omega_s^{1/2}\) (Multiple Factor Analysis scaling), \(H_s = \) spatial regularization absent. "energy": inverse Frobenius norm squared block. "none": disable block scaling (weights = 1). w_tau Shrinkage parameter (0..1) toward equal weights. 0 keeps raw weights, 1 forces equal weighting. ridge Ridge regularization parameter (default 0). rank Desired rank decomposition. NULL, uses full rank. keep_X Logical; TRUE, store concatenated training matrix used build multiblock projection (can large). available fit exact block_biprojector; q-space moments matching subject--voxel factor. cpca_blocks Optional integer vector specifying effect rows span CPCA design subspace. Ignored cpca_part = "none" cpca_T provided. cpca_T Optional qxq0 matrix giving CPCA design basis explicitly. supplied overrides cpca_blocks. cpca_part CPCA-filtered component estimate: "none" (default) performs standard DKGE fit; "design" uses CPCA design part; "resid" uses residual part; "" fits design part also stores residual basis inspection. cpca_ridge Optional ridge added CPCA-filtered matrices eigen-decomposition. weights Either NULL (default) apply weighting scheme specified w_method, dkge_weights() specification controlling additional voxel/anchor-level weighting. supplied, must inherit dkge_weights resolved via dkge_weights(). solver Solver used q-space problem. "pooled" keeps original eigen-decomposition; "jd" performs joint diagonalisation using dkge_jd_control() settings. jd_control Control parameters JD solver. jd_mask Optional mask (matrix list matrices) applied -diagonal penalty JD. supplied single matrix recycled across subjects. jd_init Optional orthogonal initialiser JD solver expressed whitened \(K^{1/2}\) metric (qxq matrix). effect_scaling Effect-space scaling applied accumulating compressed covariance. "pooled_design" (default) multiplies subject beta/effect matrix pooled design Cholesky factor, preserving original GLM-beta behavior. "none" leaves rows input scale uses identity contrast ruler, appropriate rows already common absolute interpretation AUC minus chance. effect_weights Optional dkge_effect_weights() specification. Count, explicit precision, DerSimonian-Laird "random_effects" weighting applied raw q-space effect moments pooled ruler design kernel mix effect rows. Random-effects fits q-space-. debias Finite-trial noise treatment. "none" preserves observed second moment. "analytic" subtracts noise_trace * effect_noise_cov subject pooling; sufficient statistics produced dkge_trial_subject(). "split_half" uses symmetrized cross-product two independently estimated trial halves requires dkge_trial_subject(split = ...). missingness Partial-effect coverage policy used subjects observe effect rows. "none" keeps raw zero-filled union accumulation, "rescale" divides entries observed pair counts, "mask" zeros -covered entries, "shrink" blends rescaled entries toward diagonal according coverage. policies operate raw q-space effect moments pooled ruler design kernel mix rows. effect_weights active, "none"/"mask" scale precision-weighted per-pair mean observed subject mass \(\sum_s a_s w_s 1[\mathrm{obs}_s]\) (equal full cohort mass complete coverage), "rescale" returns per-pair mean, "mask"/"shrink" threshold effective pair count $pair_ess instead raw $pair_counts. unit precision, equal subject weights, full coverage coincide unweighted policies; partial coverage keep effect-weighted mean observed-mass scale rather mean-imputing absent subjects. miss_args List arguments missingness. Known fields min_pairs (used "mask" "shrink") gamma (used "shrink"). Unknown names error. spatial Optional model-level spatial regularizer created dkge_spatial_regularizer(). sparse Laplacian resolvent used fitted moment, held-folds, components, contrasts, prediction. lambda = 0 exactly unsmoothed model.

title: dkge 0.0.0.9000
text: Model-level spatial regularization. dkge_spatial_regularizer() builds graph Laplacians adjoin (accepts precomputed Laplacians), binds shared subject-specific beta-column domains, applies sparse (+ lambda * L)^{-1} solves inside pooled moment reconstructed component, contrast, bootstrap, transport, prediction fields. regularizer can therefore change learned q-space solution rather merely blur display. lambda = 0 exactly unsmoothed fit; dkge_cv_spatial_grid() scores candidate penalties raw held-fields fixed validation geometry uses smoothest one-SE choice. Analytic noise debiasing fails closed diagonal residual-variance contract identify smoothing-induced spatial covariance; split-half debiasing remains supported. dkge_contrast_diagnostics() preflights planned contrasts fitted kernel support, reporting retained/null fractions distinct contrasts produce nearly proportional kernel queries. Numerical support tolerance now separate practical query collinearity; returned summary names maximally correlated query pair reports query-norm range. dkge_component_contrasts() constructs component-isolating contrast matrix R %*% U. makes contrast path distinct dual salience/read-basis K %*% U, must fed back contrast. dkge_signflip_maxT() now explicitly exposes max-T FWER-adjusted p per-location unadjusted p_unadj. latter raw value reported dkge_infer() p_values, p_adjusted retains max-T control; result axes carry stable subject, feature, permutation labels. partial-effect-space article restored now executes coverage, pair-ESS, weighted chunked-debiasing, estimability-warning contracts. Partial effect spaces. Subjects may observe subset design effects (observed_rows dkge_subject(); dkge_effect_grid() canonical cell grid). Coverage provenance (obs_mask, pair_counts) flows dkge_fit(), gains missingness = c("none", "mask", "rescale", "shrink") miss_args. Masking acts raw effect space R/K^{1/2} congruence; coupling kernel therefore spreads observed energy unobserved coordinates design — use block_factors design_kernel() strict separation. See ?dkge_subject ?dkge_fit. Effect-reliability weighting debiasing. dkge_effect_weights() ("none", "count", "precision") dkge_fit(debias = c("none", "analytic", "split_half")) top new central moment-pooling engine. dkge_trial_subject() dkge_trial_subject_chunks() build subjects trial-level designs sufficient statistics debiasing needs. Aggregate (cell-mean) decomposition. dkge_aggregate_target(), dkge_aggregate_fit(), dkge_aggregate_align(), dkge_aggregate_stat(), dkge_aggregate_permute(), dkge_aggregate_bootstrap(): PLS-style decomposition group--cell aggregate maps kernel metric permutation bootstrap inference (alternative, parallel). Component diagnostics plots. dkge_component_saliences(), dkge_component_contrast_scores(), dkge_design_basis(), dkge_subject_component_projections(), dkge_principal_angles_K(), dkge_plot_* counterparts. dkge_data()/dkge() gain effects= pin effect union order (e.g. dkge_effect_grid()$cell_labels). dkge_fit() reorders kernel whose dimnames permutation data’s effects errors set mismatch. dkge_fit(effect_scaling = "none") keeps effect rows input scale. dkge_between_permute() gains method = "rotation" Haar rotation reduced model’s residual space. finite-sample exact documented matrix-normal row-sphericity model, preserves crossprod(Y), fails closed weights, multiple blocks, fewer two residual dimensions. remains opt-: frozen 8,100-result audit fixed earlier Freedman–Lane null inflation global Gaussian null, missed one nuisance-null promotion gate predeclared power gates (Freedman–Lane’s raw power advantage mostly size inflation). function also gains parallel=; methods use compressed evaluation give seeded serial/parallel-identical results. dkge_subject_model() gains subject_id_col. Contrast estimability (/within/mixed) now classified structurally kernel’s factor scopes, dkge_contrast(method = "loso") warns -subject contrasts regardless named.

title: dkge 0.0.0.9000
text: Kernel roots now preserve exact positive-semidefinite support instead jittering null(K) artificial inverse directions. Fits cap latent rank rank(K), keep ridge inside image(K), expose rank/nullity/condition diagnostics, reject contrasts chosen kernel represent. Kernel cross-validation now requires full-rank candidates default scores every candidate one fixed validation geometry (identity/effect space default). Intentional quotient models require kernel_rank_policy = "allow_singular"; excluded candidates remain audit rows, score saturation flagged, preventing low-rank kernel grading directions kept. Full-rank spectrally concentrated kernels now expose participation-ratio effective rank, effective-rank fraction, leading-eigenvalue share fit, contrast, CV diagnostics. CV warns—without changing predictive selection—selected kernel effectively concentrated selected latent rank. Sinkhorn transport now separates joint couplings value-application operators. Intensive fields preserve constants, extensive values preserve total mass, fitted reliability applied twice, solve reports convergence, iteration, marginal-error, cache-hit diagnostics. Warm-start keys digest complete numerical problem non-converged states cached; legacy sinkhorn_cpp method name deprecated alias main path already uses C++. K-Procrustes now reports achieved proper-rotation objective reflections forbidden, validates PSD kernels K-orthonormal inputs, accepts arbitrary eigenvector sign reflections fold/analytic alignment, validates consensus controls. dkge_sim_toy() also samples named term blocks position, fixing scalar-sample() ambiguity plant duplicate, metric-singular components. Design-kernel metadata now declares cell effect coordinate spaces names axes cell--effect map. Kernel permutations align declared K axis; design-basis, target, plotting, classification, estimability consumers rematch names fail closed ambiguous mappings. particular, equal cell/effect dimensions longer treated proof cell metadata indexes effect rows. Analytic LOSO now reports structural fallback causes numerical ones. Pair-normalized effect/missingness pooling labeled pair_normalized_pooling, covariance-aware moments labeled covariance_aware_moment, later large perturbation mask either primary cause. dkge_procrustes_K() returned transpose optimal rotation; error invisible rank ≤ 2 (transpositions involutions) permuted components rank ≥ 3. K-Procrustes call sites (bootstrap, analytic, folds, aggregate alignment, neuralign adapter) affected. design_kernel(): RBF length-scale read f$l, partially matched f$levels, breaking ordinal/circular/continuous factors carrying level labels. dkge_data() now rejects duplicate subject IDs. dkge_subject(), dkge_data(), union-alignment path now reject duplicated effect labels instead dropping beta row. dkge_aggregate_permute() evaluates statistic unaligned null refit (alignment diagnostic ). dkge_aggregate_bootstrap() gains interval = c("percentile", "basic") returns excludes_zero = NA non-negative "singular_value" statistic. dkge_aggregate_target() keeps inferred cell factor cell_data = NULL, matches rows/columns name, warns unused values names. Chunked trial subjects longer let unweighted noise_trace short-circuit analytic debiasing Omega voxel weights present. Rescale/shrink missingness divide subject-weight mass (pair_weight) rather unweighted pair counts; none/mask restore observed pair mass partial coverage (S/k inflation). dkge_between_permute(terms = NULL) skips terms listed design$nuisance. Rotation accepts factor unused block levels. dkge_subject_model(na.action = na.omit) keeps subject IDs aligned retained rows. Subject weights default w_method = "mfa_sigma1" retain legacy power-iteration numerical contract inside frozen private RNG scope. Fits reproducible leave caller’s RNG unchanged, matching canonical pre-extension default weights downstream results. Contrast estimability now prefers structural evidence contrast’s name, -subject contrast named within-subject term still flagged. dkge_update_weights() refits now preserve effect_scaling, effect_weights, debias, missingness, miss_args.

title: dkge 0.0.0.9000
text: kernel_roots() now defaults jitter = 0 returns Moore–Penrose inverse square root singular kernels. positive jitter explicitly regularizes K; longer happens invisibly every call. dkge_cv_*() scores therefore comparable across kernels numerically interchangeable former candidate-specific K-metric scores. design_kernel(terms = NULL) one-factor design now contains main-effect term . Previously identical main effect full interaction added, doubled unnormalized cell kernel duplicated effect-basis block labels. Multi-factor defaults unchanged; callers intentionally need old cell-kernel scale can set sole term’s rho 2 explicitly. Cross-fitting helpers (dkge_loso_contrast(), dkge_cv_*, k-fold builders) now inherit missingness fit instead defaulting "none". Numerically identical full-coverage fits. dkge_design_basis() / dkge_component_contrast_scores() default normalize = "unit_K" (unit K-norm) instead unit Euclidean norm; dkge_component_saliences(scale = "unit") now means unit K-norm. fit$subjects longer retains per-subject beta/design/omega (debiasing sufficient statistics); fit$effect_moments_raw aliases fit$effect_moments fit$noise_moments NULL debias = "none". New arguments dkge_fit(), dkge(), dkge_subject_model() appended pre-existing ones; positional calls earlier releases unaffected. dkge_make_target(type = "transported_maps", centroids = NULL) now keeps every supplied contrast (previously contrasts first silently dropped) labels features <contrast>:<index>, ncol(Y) grows number contrasts. dkge_fit(): design kernel whose labels reconciled data’s effect names (duplicated labels) now warns; kernel rownames != colnames error. dkge_weights() now errors subjects different numbers voxels/clusters instead silently recycling one subject’s weights onto another. Roxygen markdown mode enabled package-wide (documentation now renders cross-reference links code spans correctly).
